description: Deterministic disease information lookup used after CNN prediction.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Small brown to dark spots on leaves
Yellow halos may surround leaf spots
Spots can occur on stems and fruit
Fruit may develop raised, corky or scabby spots
prevention: Use pathogen-free seed and healthy transplants
Keep foliage as dry as practical
Maintain good plant spacing and airflow
Remove crop debris after the season
Rotate away from tomato and pepper
cultural_management: Use drip, furrow or soil-level irrigation
Avoid working with plants when foliage is wet
Remove severely affected plant material where appropriate
Control volunteer tomato and pepper plants
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.source: UC IPM / University of Minnesota Extension

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Early Blight
symptoms: Dark brown spots usually begin on older lower leaves
Larger lesions may show concentric rings
Yellow tissue may surround lesions
Severe infection can cause leaf drop
Stem lesions may also show dark concentric rings
prevention: Rotate away from tomato and related crops
Control tomato volunteers and susceptible weeds
Use mulch to reduce soil splash
cultural_management: Water at the base of plants
Sanitize tools after handling infected plants
Remove or bury crop residue after harvest

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Late Blight
symptoms: Large dark brown or green-brown blotches on leaves
Lesions may have green-gray edges
Stems and petioles may become dark brown
White growth may appear under humid conditions
Fruit can develop firm dark brown lesions
prevention: Monitor plants during cool and wet conditions
Remove volunteer plants and infected crop material
cultural_management: Avoid handling plants when foliage is wet
Monitor surrounding tomato and potato crops

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.name: Tomato Leaf Mold
symptoms: Pale yellow or greenish-yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces
Olive-green to brown velvety growth on lower leaf surfaces
Older leaves are commonly affected first
Affected leaves may wither and die

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Septoria Leaf Spot
symptoms: Small circular leaf spots
Spots commonly have dark margins
Centers may be tan or gray
Small dark structures may develop in the centers
Lower leaves are commonly affected first
prevention: Use mulch to reduce soil splash
Do not save seed from infected plants
cultural_management: Water at the base of plants
Remove affected lower leaves when appropriate

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Two-Spotted Spider Mites
symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling on leaves
Leaves may become mottled or bronzed
Heavy feeding can cause leaf decline
Fine webbing may appear with larger infestations
prevention: Pay particular attention during hot and dry conditions
cultural_management: Remove heavily damaged leaves where appropriate
Use physical washing of foliage when suitable

Tomato___Target_Spot.name: Target Spot
symptoms: Brown to dark lesions on leaves
Lesions may develop concentric target-like rings
Disease can cause defoliation
Fruit may develop sunken or damaged spots
prevention: Start with clean and healthy transplants
Remove plant debris that can harbor inoculum

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
symptoms: Leaves become small and curl upward
Strong yellowing between and along leaf veins
Leaves may become crumpled
Plants may become severely stunted
Internodes may become shortened
Flower development and fruit production may be reduced
prevention: Avoid planting near infected older tomato fields where practical
cultural_management: Remove infected plants when appropriate and infection incidence is low
Remove old crop residue and volunteer plants
Use physical barriers such as fine mesh where appropriate

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves
Leaves may curl or become malformed
Plants may become stunted
Fruit may show uneven ripening or abnormal coloration
prevention: Avoid spreading plant sap between plants
Remove infected plants to reduce sources of infection
cultural_management: Sanitize tools after working with infected plants
Control volunteer and weed hosts where relevant
Avoid handling healthy plants immediately after infected plants
Do not expect a chemical cure for an infected plant

Tomato___healthy.name: Healthy
symptoms: No clear disease pattern detected
No characteristic disease symptoms identified by the model
prevention: Maintain suitable irrigation and plant spacing
cultural_management: Water at the soil level where practical
Remove diseased plant material if symptoms appear
